title: Fix multi-page plateau: inter-hop settle delay + ANSI/padding-noise-robust richness comparison
action: User field-test finding (2026-07-28): multi-page (cell -5) plateaued after 2 hops regardless of requested depth; live investigation across 2 real Claude Code panes (w3:p6, w8:p1, chosen because they were genuinely idle -- workspace_status idle, confirmed stable across a 1s re-read before testing) found two compounding bugs. (1) Firing the next hop's PageUp with only the fast per-attempt interval (40ms) after the previous hop landed sometimes caught the agent's TUI mid-transition from THAT hop, producing a shorter/degraded read for the next one instead of a genuinely deeper one -- fixed with a longer dedicated INTER_HOP_SETTLE (150ms) before each subsequent PageUp, and by no longer overwriting the accepted `escalated` content with a hop that didn't land richer (previously it did, silently regressing the returned content). (2) is_richer's raw `.text.len()` comparison is fundamentally noisy against real Claude Code panes: their own footer (live elapsed-time/token-percentage counters) re-renders on every single read regardless of scroll position, and ANSI color codes plus right-padding to the terminal's column width both swing raw length independent of actual content -- on one real pane (w8:p1) this was enough to make a genuinely richer escalation register as 'not richer', plateauing at hop 1. Fixed by comparing a new `visible_len` (ANSI-stripped, each line's trailing whitespace trimmed) instead of raw byte length. Live re-test after both fixes: w8:p1 now correctly progresses to depth 2 (previously plateaued at depth 1 immediately); w3:p6 still plateaus after ~2 hops but the remaining depth-3-vs-2 delta is now only a few characters (consistent with residual footer-digit noise, e.g. a percentage crossing a digit boundary, not a scrolling bug) rather than the large swings seen before either fix. A full elimination of that residual noise floor (e.g. excluding a known footer region) was explicitly NOT attempted -- doing so would mean encoding Claude-Code-specific geometry knowledge into PaneScroller, contradicting this feature's own D3 (never branch on agent identity/features). Left as a known, disclosed limitation.

truths: a hop that doesn't land richer never overwrites the previously-accepted (richer) escalated content
there is a dedicated, longer settle delay between accepting one hop and firing the next hop's PageUp, separate from the fast per-attempt poll interval
richness comparison ignores ANSI CSI escape sequences and each line's trailing whitespace padding, not just raw byte length
existing single-hop and NativeScrollback-vs-EscapeInjection behavior is unchanged for plain text with no ANSI/padding noise

artifacts.substantive: INTER_HOP_SETTLE constant + corrected non-richer handling; visible_len() ANSI/padding-aware length helper backing is_richer(); 4 new unit tests (2 for visible_len, 1 for is_richer noise robustness, plus the settle/non-overwrite behavior covered by existing multi-page tests still passing)

key_links: is_richer's signature and all existing call sites unchanged -- only its internal comparison basis changed from .text.len() to visible_len()
prohibitions: no agent-name/kind branching to work around footer noise (would violate D3)
no change to the always-restore-to-live guarantee
